issues.summary: All-or-nothing safeParse drops every message and the traceId when one errors[] entry is malformed
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: rhinestone-error.schema.ts:20-21 declares `errors: z.array(z.object({ message: z.string() }))`. If any single entry lacks a string message, or errors is null, safeParse fails and rhinestone-api.service.ts:112-113 returns '' with no traceId either. That is a real loss of diagnostics, but only for a body that doesn't match Rhinestone's documented shape.

issues.summary: No tests for a malformed errors[] entry or a traceId-only body
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: The five new spec cases (spec.ts:157-279) all pass well-formed errors[] arrays, and only the first one includes a traceId. The degraded-body path at service.ts:112 and the traceId-without-messages path at service.ts:125 are never exercised.

issues.summary: getTaskStatus's newly enriched error log is not tested
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: getTaskStatus logs through the same formatError (service.ts:214), but every new test goes through relay(). The helper is shared, so a regression that affects only getTaskStatus is unlikely.

issues.summary: Upstream free-text errors[].message can still echo addresses into logs, even though the comment says request details are kept out
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: service.ts:116-123 copies errors[].message verbatim up to 200 chars, and the doc comment at :100-105 presents the dropping of context as keeping addresses out of log storage. If Rhinestone embeds an address in the message, it still gets logged. The PR deliberately accepts messages, so this is a doc/policy gap rather than a defect.

issues.summary: Unescaped double quotes let an upstream message forge a traceId= field inside the log fragment
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: service.ts:123 wraps the joined messages in `"..."` without escaping, and truncateForLog (:136-141) only collapses whitespace. A message like `x" traceId=abc` therefore yields a misleading field in the log line. The impact is limited to misleading grep/parse of a free-text log.

issues.summary: Messages are sliced before the empty-string filter, so whitespace-only leading entries can crowd out real ones
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: service.ts:116-119 runs `.slice(0, 3)` before `.filter(m => m.length > 0)`, so three blank entries followed by a real message would log nothing. The logic is correct as described, but the scenario is unlikely in practice.

issues.summary: The log-forging rationale for collapsing newlines is weak because the production logger's JSON format already escapes newlines
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: logging.module.ts:40 uses winston.format.json() outside pretty mode, and JSON escapes \n, so newlines cannot split a production log line. The collapsing is still harmless and useful for readability, so this is only a comment accuracy issue.

issues.summary: Four new tests hard-code status 400 / 'Bad Request' instead of generating them with faker
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: spec.ts: the four tests after the first new one use `{ status: 400, statusText: 'Bad Request' }`, while the first new test and the existing tests use faker, and testing.md:70 prefers faker except at assertion boundaries. In the 'keep detail out' test the 400 is arguably that boundary; elsewhere this is only a consistency issue with no functional cost.

issues.summary: The exported RhinestoneErrorResponse type has no importers
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: grep finds RhinestoneErrorResponse only at its definition, rhinestone-error.schema.ts:24. The service imports only the schema. Exporting the inferred type is the sibling-schema convention, so the cost is negligible.

issues.summary: The new schema has no dedicated spec file, unlike tenderly-simulation.schema
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: schemas/__tests__/ contains only tenderly-simulation.schema.spec.ts. The new schema is a trivial all-optional object and is exercised indirectly through the service spec.

issues.summary: Suggestion to extract the pure helper methods from the class for isolated testing
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: describeUpstreamError and truncateForLog (service.ts:110-141) use no instance state apart from calling each other through `this`. Moving them out is a structural preference, and the existing tests cover them adequately through relay().
